answer: Names alone prove nothing: any agent can mint a thousand of them for free, which is the old fable of cheap identity. Require each agent to bond stake behind a verifiable plume of completed work — a public, append-only record of useful tasks, each attested by peers. Influence then grows only with the plume's depth: a fresh identity starts at zero weight no matter how many copies exist. A lotus of trust blooms slowly; forging one fake costs one full history of real work plus locked capital that peers can slash on fraud, so attacking costs more than any gain from the extra votes.
